market_holds: Spot $139.17 at the 2026-11-23 close (sealed baseline). The front-expiry straddle implies 9.47%, or 8.21% for the event once ordinary volatility is netted out. 25-delta skew is +21.7 vol points toward puts, so downside protection is bid. Run-up: +11.4% over 20 days and +0.3% over 5. The stock sits 5.3% below its 52-week high ($148.54 on about Nov 4, per StockStory) and has risen about 15% since the Q2 print, when it fell 3.9% to $126.75 on a soft Q3 EPS guide. The last 7 reactions have a median absolute move of 6.4%: 4 up and 3 down, including +17.9% on Q1 and -3.9% on Q2. Q3 guide (2026-08-27): comps +3% to +4%, revenue $5.00B to $5.10B, adjusted EPS $0.80 to $0.95 after a roughly $0.50 drag from reinvesting tariff refunds. FY adjusted EPS guide is $7.70 to $8.05, including about $0.60 of net tariff benefit, and FY comps +3% to +4%. Consensus is $0.88 EPS on $5.05B (Earnings Whispers preview via finviz, 2026-11-16), which is the guide midpoint, so it is anchored on the guide. The whisper is $1.06, above the top of the range. I found no published quarterly comp consensus. Short interest rose from 7.24M shares (2026-09-30) to 9.72M (10-15) and 10.02M (10-30), or 5.4 days to cover (Nasdaq). Shorts were building into the rally. Management told the market at Q2 that Q4 gross margin would fall year over year on fuel-driven freight surcharges.
view: The quarter itself probably beats on the line the stock trades on, which is traffic, then comps. Placer.ai's same-store visits for Dollar Tree ran -0.6% in March and -3.5% in April 2026, against a reported Q1 traffic decline of 1.0%. They flipped to +4.8% in July against reported Q2 traffic of +0.4%. Placer puts calendar Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) at +4.9%, against +1.2% for Dollar General (article dated 2026-11-23). On the Q1 and Q2 mapping that points to reported fiscal Q3 traffic of about +2% to +4%, a sharp acceleration. Ticket has been +3% to +4.5%, so the comp likely lands above the 3-4% guide. Target's traffic was +5% in its October quarter, so value and mass retail were strong in the period, while Walmart US comps were +2.9%. The $210M reinvestment was aimed at exactly this traffic. Seeing it work is the story bulls have been waiting for. But the tape already leans that way: the stock is up about 15% since the Q2 print, the whisper sits above the guide, and Placer's quarterly data was in subscribers' hands weeks ago. A Q3 beat on comps and EPS is close to the base case. The reaction will turn on the FY/Q4 guide, specifically how much of the Q3 beat passes through and whether management cuts Q4 margins for freight. Diesel averaged $5.96 over Aug-Oct 2026, against $3.73 a year earlier and $5.19 in May-Jul. It peaked at $6.53 in late September, above the roughly $5.6 level when the guide was set (FRED GASDESW). The Q2 print is the cautionary pattern: a beat and an FY raise, and the stock still fell on the next-quarter guide. Two things tilt the asymmetry modestly upward against that: shorts built about 38% in October and put skew is heavy. A clean traffic beat with an FY raise likely squeezes. A held FY guide with a fuel-margin warning likely gives back part of the run. I lean up, at about 60%, which is not enough to act on.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the traffic acceleration. Sell-side consensus revenue and EPS sit exactly at the guide midpoints, so they were not revised for Placer's +4.9% calendar-Q3 visits. Rising short interest and +21.7-point put skew suggest positioning leans against a clean beat. The bias is anchoring on the company's guide after independent data moved. The offset is that the buy side reads Placer and the stock is up about 15% since Q2, so much of this is probably held.

recommendation.reason: The independent traffic data (Placer +4.9% same-store visits for calendar Q3, after a negative H1) points to a comp beat against the guide-anchored consensus. Building short interest and heavy put skew add some squeeze asymmetry. But the stock is up about 15% since Q2 and the whisper is above the guide range. The reaction turns on the FY/Q4 guide, where diesel 60% higher year over year and the flagged Q4 gross-margin decline give management reason to stay cautious. The Q2 precedent was a beat-and-raise that still fell. Probability is below the 65 needed to act.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Reported Q3 traffic flat or negative despite the Placer reading, or an FY EPS guide that is not raised by at least the Q3 beat because of freight and fuel margin pressure in Q4.

self_critique: The traffic acceleration is the most-watched datapoint on this name and Placer is widely subscribed, so the 15% rally since Q2 and the $1.06 whisper may already exceed what a comp beat can deliver. Dollar Tree has sold off on beat-and-raise prints when the forward guide disappointed (Q2 2026, -3.9%). Q4 carries visible pressure from fuel, freight, reinvestment and holiday mix that could make the FY guide look like a hold. Placer visits also diverged from reported traffic by 1-4 points in recent quarters, so the comp beat may be smaller than mapped.
approach_notes: P3's freshest-data-first and own-arithmetic calibration of Placer against reported traffic was the most useful step, and P6's guide-is-the-line framing kept the view near 60 instead of chasing the traffic beat. P4's 'priced is a claim to prove' cut both ways here: the consensus is provably stale against the data, but the run-up and whisper suggest the buy side holds it.
